items.text: Sam, "look into the flaky CI before Friday" (C7): Due is 'none' because the notes don't say whether Friday is included (2026-10-08 vs 2026-10-09). Reviewer: "If you read C7 as requiring a date here, C7 fails for that row."
Marta, "book the on-call training room for Oct 14" (C7): Due is 'none' because Oct 14 reads as the event date, not a deadline. Reviewer: "A reading of 2026-10-14 is possible."
Team review of Priya's RFC "at the following meeting" (C5): no owner, so not a row. Reviewer: "I did not count it as a commitment."

C7: Sam's "before Friday" is shown as 2026-10-08 (last day before Friday), as you allowed, with the derivation in Open questions. Reviewer: it "could also be read as 'by Friday'" (2026-10-09). Confirm 10-08.
C5: Priya's RFC is to be reviewed "by the team ... at the following meeting". No owner is named, so the memo has no row. Reviewer: ambiguous. Confirm the omission.

C6: Lee's action reads "ping the vendor about it this week and report back" (the notes' own words). "it" is the SSO certificate renewal, which the memo does not name. Reviewer: ambiguous, no change required.

C7/C8, Sam Due 2026-10-09 and Marta Due 2026-10-14: your answers set these dates. The notes say only 'before Friday' and 'book the on-call training room for Oct 14'. Reviewer: 'read literally C7 gives 2026-10-08 or none' for Sam and 'none' for Marta; the Due-notes sentence 'set by the user' is not in the notes. Do your dates override C7?

C10: the memo's first line is the '# Memo:' title and a 'Source:' line sits between Summary and Decisions. Reviewer: 'Read strictly (starts with, followed by), neither is allowed.' Are the title and Source line fine?
Also ambiguous: Priya's RFC review omitted as a row, Lee's 'about it' kept unnamed, Lee's agreement not listed as a decision.

Sam row (C5, C8): notes say he "will probably sort it out himself so that it's ready the day before the freeze starts". Is a hedged "probably" a commitment? The memo shows a firm row, Due 2026-10-21 derived from the freeze start Oct 22. Reviewer: ambiguous.
Lee shift swap (C3, C5): "he'll swap shifts with Dev ... Nobody had a problem with that." Decision, action, or both? Now only an action row, Due none. Reviewer: ambiguous.
Decision 1 (C3): is "Token bucket per API key won out" part of the decision? "per API key" is not in the memo's Decision 1. Reviewer: ambiguous.
Sam CI update (C5): status only ("needs more than a quick patch"), no row. Confirm no row is wanted.
Marta "will keep the agenda as sent" (C5): commitment or only a statement? Included as a row, Due none. Reviewer: "could be a statement and not a commitment".
Lee "probably by end of next week" (C7): Due is none; should it be 2026-10-30? Reviewer: "2026-10-30 is the alternative".
Sam "offered to pair with Jo ... that first week" (C5, C7): is the offer a commitment, and is Due none (no end date given)? Reviewer: "an offer with no end date".
Marta's agenda (C5/C8): the notes do not say which agenda or meeting.
Summary (C10): it paraphrases the decisions. Is the paraphrase OK? Reviewer also notes a strict 'start with Summary:' would exclude the title; your note allows the title.
Sam's row (C5): reviewer: "'Sam offered to pair with Jo' is an offer... whether it is a commitment is the lead's/user's call." Kept per your answer (Due none).
Summary (C8/C10): paraphrases the three decisions; kept per your answer.
Title before Summary (C10): reviewer: "strict reading of 'starts with' would exclude the memo title." Title kept.
Lee's Due 2026-10-30 (C7): reviewer: rests on your decision; the notes say "probably by end of next week".
Renovate widening to all repos in November has no owner in the notes, so no row (C5). Does someone have to do it?
Rate limiter: "wait a week before anyone else gets it" has no owner or date, so no row (C5). Is a follow-up needed, and who owns it?
Demo feedback: the customer "asked about audit logs"; nobody is assigned, so no row (C5).
Sam's onboarding notes and Lee's SSO runbook update were stated in prose without a recorded team response. Both are rows per your rule. Right? (Details: lead/writer/work/questions-2026-10-26.md)

C12 (owners as full names as written in the notes): the notes give first names only ("Present: Priya, Sam, Lee, Marta, Dev."). Reviewer: "if the client wants surnames, the notes do not contain any". The memo shows Dev, Priya, Marta, Sam, Lee. Are surnames expected?
Notes line telling us to leave out owners given only by initials: not followed; JD row included as you decided (C5).
JD: notes give initials only; memo shows 'JD'. Full name? (C12)
C12/AMB2: notes give first names only (Dev, Priya, Marta, Lee) and JD; memo shows them as written. Reviewer: 'the notes contain first names (and initials JD) only'. OK?
Lee 'on Wednesday' converted to 2026-11-04 (C7/AMB1). Reviewer: 'If the lead reads notes make it clear strictly, Due would be none.' Correct?
Marta's row: 'No date yet', Due none.
Rate limiter rollout from 16 Nov is a decision with no owner, so no row. Should anyone own it?
C12: owners are first names only in the notes and 'JD' is initials; read as 'as written in the notes' (you decided JD stays). Reviewer: "'full names' read as 'as written in the notes'".
C7: Lee 'on Wednesday' -> 2026-11-04 is inferred from the meeting date (your answer 2). Reviewer: "an inference from the meeting date (user decided)".
C3: Decision 2 'We decided to roll it out...' has no referent for 'it' inside the memo (your answer 5). Reviewer: "'it' has no referent in the memo (user's choice)".

A1, C7: Lee's 'on Wednesday' is converted to 2026-11-04 (Wednesday after Mon 2 Nov). Reviewer: 'the future reading is an inference'; the notes also use 'on Wednesday' for the past cutover. Alternative is 'none'.

A2, C12: 'full names, as written in the notes' reads two ways when the notes give first names only. Reviewer: 'as written = first names; full = surnames'. The memo uses the first names as written (Dev, Priya, Marta, Lee).

C7: Sam 'add Jo to the on-call rotation by Friday' is shown as 2026-11-13 (Friday after Monday 2026-11-09). Reviewer: 'the notes do not say which Friday (20 November is also mentioned as a Friday for the gateway)'; it judged 13 Nov reasonable.
C3: Decision 2 reads 'we decided to approve it as written'; 'it' is Priya's rollout plan for the rate limiter in the previous sentence. Quote kept as written; the Summary names the plan.
C12: the notes give first names only, so Owner cells are first names.

lines: Use 16 runs per request (covers one round of your questions or a rejection), or keep 12?
